original_question: Let (a_n(ω)) and (b_n(ω)) be two independent random sequences built from selection probabilities n^{-a} and n^{-b} with a, b ∈ (0,1) and a ≠ b. Is it almost surely true that for every system (X, X, µ, T, S) and bounded functions f, g, the averages (1/N) Σ T^{a_n(ω)} f · S^{b_n(ω)} g converge, in L2 or pointwise, to E(f | I_T) · E(g | I_S)?
target_in_paper: Section 7, Problem 33: the question about bilinear ergodic averages along two independently generated random subsequences with different exponents a and b. ([math.uoc.gr](https://www.math.uoc.gr/~nikosf/OpenProblems/OpenProblems.pdf?utm_source=openai))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core of Problem 33 quite well: it uses two independent random sequences selected with probabilities n^{-a} and n^{-b}, assumes a,b\in(0,1) with a\neq b, quantifies over a common dynamical system and bounded observables, and asks whether the averages converge to E(f|I_T)\cdot E(g|I_S) in L^2 or pointwise. That is exactly the paper’s intended target. ([math.uoc.gr](https://www.math.uoc.gr/~nikosf/OpenProblems/OpenProblems.pdf?utm_source=openai))
missing_details: The paper does not speak only abstractly of 'random sequences built from selection probabilities'; it specifies mutually independent 0-1 Bernoulli variables X_1,Y_1,X_2,Y_2,\dots with P(X_n=1)=n^{-a} and P(Y_n=1)=n^{-b}. ([math.uoc.gr](https://www.math.uoc.gr/~nikosf/OpenProblems/OpenProblems.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The sequences a_n(\omega) and b_n(\omega) are the increasing enumerations of the selected integers \{m\in\mathbb N:X_m(\omega)=1\} and \{m\in\mathbb N:Y_m(\omega)=1\}; this construction should be stated explicitly. ([math.uoc.gr](https://www.math.uoc.gr/~nikosf/OpenProblems/OpenProblems.pdf?utm_source=openai))

'Almost surely' is used in the paper in a strong uniform sense: there should exist a universal full-measure set \Omega_0 such that every \omega\in\Omega_0 works simultaneously for all systems and all f,g. Your draft does not spell out this universal-set quantifier. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/OpenProblems/OpenProblems.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The ambient dynamical object is a probability space (X,\mathcal X,\mu) together with commuting invertible measure-preserving transformations T,S:X\to X; your shorthand '(X, X, \mu, T, S)' leaves 'probability', 'commuting', 'invertible', and 'measure-preserving' implicit. ([math.uoc.gr](https://www.math.uoc.gr/~nikosf/OpenProblems/OpenProblems.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The paper requires f,g\in L^\infty(\mu), not just informally 'bounded functions'; for a stand-alone version it is cleaner to say bounded measurable functions, equivalently elements of L^\infty(\mu). ([math.uoc.gr](https://www.math.uoc.gr/~nikosf/OpenProblems/OpenProblems.pdf?utm_source=openai))

For a self-contained formulation, the Koopman-action notation should be unpacked: T^m f means f\circ T^m and S^m g means g\circ S^m. This convention is part of the paper’s general framework. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/OpenProblems/OpenProblems.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The notation I_T and I_S should be explained explicitly as the T-invariant and S-invariant \sigma-algebras; the paper uses this shorthand in the statement without re-explaining it locally. ([math.uoc.gr](https://www.math.uoc.gr/~nikosf/OpenProblems/OpenProblems.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The paper imposes only a\neq b; it does not assume an ordering such as a<b. A stand-alone rewrite should preserve that exact scope. ([math.uoc.gr](https://www.math.uoc.gr/~nikosf/OpenProblems/OpenProblems.pdf?utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Let (\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P) support mutually independent Bernoulli random variables X_1,Y_1,X_2,Y_2,\dots with \mathbb P(X_n=1)=n^{-a} and \mathbb P(Y_n=1)=n^{-b}, where a,b\in(0,1) and a\neq b. For each \omega\in\Omega, let a_n(\omega) and b_n(\omega) be the increasing enumerations of \{m\in\mathbb N:X_m(\omega)=1\} and \{m\in\mathbb N:Y_m(\omega)=1\}. Is it true that there exists a set \Omega_0\in\mathcal F with \mathbb P(\Omega_0)=1 such that, for every \omega\in\Omega_0, every probability space (X,\mathcal X,\mu), every pair of commuting invertible measure-preserving transformations T,S:X\to X, and every f,g\in L^\infty(\mu), the averages (1/N)\sum_{n=1}^N T^{a_n(\omega)}f\cdot S^{b_n(\omega)}g converge in L^2(\mu) — or, in the stronger version, pointwise — to E(f\mid I_T)\,E(g\mid I_S), where I_T and I_S are the T-invariant and S-invariant \sigma-algebras? ([math.uoc.gr](https://www.math.uoc.gr/~nikosf/OpenProblems/OpenProblems.pdf?utm_source=openai))
justification: This is Problem 33, not neighboring Problems 31 or 32. Problem 31 asks about multiple convergence along one random sequence, and Problem 32 mixes one deterministic iterate with one random iterate; only Problem 33 matches your draft’s combination of two independently chosen random subsequences with distinct exponents and the specific limit E(f|I_T)E(g|I_S). Section 7 immediately preceding Problem 33 supplies the Bernoulli construction of the random sequences and the paper’s uniform meaning of 'almost surely', while Section 1.2 supplies the global system/Koopman notation. ([math.uoc.gr](https://www.math.uoc.gr/~nikosf/OpenProblems/OpenProblems.pdf?utm_source=openai))
